newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM aluminium futures end firmer in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM aluminium futures end firmer in dull trade.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures ended firmer in thin trade on Monday, with many players sidelined in the absence of fresh factors, traders said.
"Volume is even thinner than usual," said one trader. "LME prices and the dollar moved little. So yen-based contracts came to a standstill."
Traders said the launch of the June contract last week failed to attract players because turnover remained very low.
June added one yen to end at 188.1 yen while April advanced 1.1 to 189.5 yen, both with volume of about 400 lots. Others gained 0.3 to 0.6 yen. Total volume was 1,040 lots.

On Friday in London, the benchmark three-month aluminium finished down $2 at $1,575 per tonne after a fairly nondescript day, while zinc reached a new 6-3/4 year high and nickel slumped to a 6-1/2 month low.
